{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"77d4feec8f2c581ae5b53930122699a962d00ac8eb1775096361f3e4257d93fe","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:51","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving Habits, Distracted and Defensive Driving, Trip Preparation and Safety Belts","heading":"C2 — KG hints for Driving Habits, Distracted and Defensive Driving, Trip Preparation and Safety Belts","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — KG hints for Driving Habits, Distracted and Defensive Driving, Trip Preparation and Safety Belts

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A02
The impatient driver is simply in a hurry, while the arrogant driver is purposely in a hurry and competes with the vehicle as an extension of ego [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint bad-habits; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F05 and sec12-F08.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
Laziness shrinks the look-behind and drops the signal, while inattention loosens the grip and lets the eyes and the vehicle wander [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint bad-habits; prereq_hint sec12-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec12-F03 and sec12-F06.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A05
Belts make a crash survivable up to sixty miles per hour, while going unbelted can be fatal at only twelve miles per hour [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint belt-numbers; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec12-F26 and sec12-F30.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A05
The lap belt sits snug across the hip bones, while the shoulder belt stays loose enough to admit a fist between belt and chest [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint belt-fit; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F28 and sec12-F25.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A04
A yellow lamp that stays lit after the computer check is a warning, while a red lamp means danger that must be checked immediately [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint warning-lamps; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F23 and sec12-F24.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A03
Hands-free equipment still leaves a phone call distracting, while pulling over in a safe place is the manual's only acceptable way to take the call [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint distraction; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F14 and sec12-F12.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A06
The car's collision takes about one tenth of a second, while the unbelted person's human collision takes about one hundredth of a second and begins one fiftieth of a second after the car stops [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint collision-timeline; prereq_hint sec12-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec12-F31 and sec12-F30.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A03
Defensive driving defends against other drivers' aggression, carelessness and intoxication, while a driver who shows those traits must first defend against himself [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint defensive-driving; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec12-F15 and sec12-F16.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A04
Scanning keeps most attention far ahead with regular glances aside, in the mirror and at the panel, while sightseeing, daydreaming and looking inside the vehicle are the distractions it excludes [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint attentiveness; prereq_hint sec12-R08; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F18 and sec12-F17.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A07
An infant rides rearward in an infant seat or a convertible seat in the infant position, while facing an infant forward is a listed common mistake [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint child-seats; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec12-F33 and sec12-F35.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A04
Fluids, tires and lamps unchecked within the past week are checked before a trip, while an unfamiliar vehicle calls for a few minutes locating its signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector and horn [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint vehicle-condition; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F20 and sec12-F21.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A03
Keeping the stereo low preserves your hearing of sirens and horns, while headsets over or in both ears are forbidden outright while driving [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint distraction; prereq_hint sec12-R06; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec12-F13 and sec12-F14.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0059]
